newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel denies report of Moody's rating cut.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel denies report of Moody's rating cut.

text.p: The Bank of Israel denied a report that it had received a letter from Moody's warning of a possible lowering of its sovereign credit rating.
"We did not get any letter. We think it is just rumours on the (Tel Aviv) market," a central bank spokesman said.
He noted that Moody's does not usually send letters of this sort. Rather, it sends a delegation to study the economy and then issues a report, he said.
Israel is rated A3 by Moody's and A-minus by Standard & Poor's.

A report in the Maariv daily said government officials feared Israel's credit rating would be reduced because of widening deficits in the budget and the balance of payments current account. The newspaper cited a report in a fax newsletter that circulates among traders that Moody's had sent a warning to the central bank.

"There is no doubt the Israeli economy is facing problems, like the budget and current account deficits. These must be dealt with. But the story with Moody's is just rumours," the central bank spokesman said.
Treasury officials could not be reached for comment.
